faqs.q: On which date was the Planning Commission scrapped by the Government of India?
On which date was the NITI Aayog established as successor to the Planning Commission?
NITI Aayog stands for which of the following?

options.c: National Innovation and Technology Institute of India

faqs.q: Like the erstwhile Planning Commission, the NITI Aayog was created by which of the following?

options.b: An executive resolution of the Union Cabinet

faqs.a: An executive resolution of the Union Cabinet
faqs.e: Being created by executive resolution, NITI Aayog is neither a constitutional body nor a statutory body.

faqs.q: Who is the Chairperson of the NITI Aayog?

Consider the following statements regarding the Governing Council of the NITI Aayog:
(I) It comprises the Chief Ministers of all the States.
(II) It comprises the Chief Ministers of Union Territories with Legislatures.
(III) It comprises the Lt. Governors of Union Territories without Legislatures.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
Who appoints the Vice-Chairperson of the NITI Aayog?
The Vice-Chairperson of the NITI Aayog enjoys the rank of which of the following?

options.d: Secretary to the Government of India

faqs.q: Full-time Members of the NITI Aayog enjoy the rank of which of the following?

options.b: Secretary to the Government of India

faqs.q: What is the maximum number of Part-time Members permitted in the NITI Aayog's full-time organisational framework?
What is the maximum number of Ex-Officio Members (from the Union Council of Ministers) permitted in the NITI Aayog?
The Chief Executive Officer of the NITI Aayog is appointed by whom, and holds the rank of which office?

options.c: Prime Minister; Secretary to the Government of India

faqs.a: Prime Minister; Secretary to the Government of India

faqs.q: Regional Councils of the NITI Aayog are formed to address issues impacting more than one state or region and are convened by whom?
Which of the following best describes an objective of the NITI Aayog?

options.a: To allocate plan and non-plan expenditure to states
options.b: To fix the borrowing limits of state governments
options.c: To evolve a shared vision of national development priorities with the active involvement of States
options.d: To formulate a centralised five-year plan for all states

faqs.a: To evolve a shared vision of national development priorities with the active involvement of States

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the functions of the NITI Aayog:
(I) Its functions can be divided into four main heads, including policy and programme framework and monitoring and evaluation.
(II) Its entire gamut of activities is divided into two main hubs — Team India, and Knowledge and Innovation.
(III) It has the sole executive authority to implement plans without state government involvement.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: NITI Aayog is a think tank providing advisory input; implementation responsibility rests with Central and State Governments, not NITI Aayog itself.

faqs.q: The 'Team India Hub' of the NITI Aayog is primarily responsible for which of the following?

options.d: Fostering cooperative federalism and designing policy and programme frameworks

faqs.a: Fostering cooperative federalism and designing policy and programme frameworks

faqs.q: Which of the following guiding principles of the NITI Aayog draws on Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay's idea of prioritising service and uplift of the poor and marginalised?
Which of the following indices has been launched by the NITI Aayog to promote competitive federalism among states?
faqs.e: NITI Aayog has launched several such indices, including the School Education Quality Index and Composite Water Management Index, to encourage healthy competition among states.

faqs.q: The NITI Aayog has launched the Aspirational Districts Programme as part of which of its initiatives?
faqs.e: The programme aims at the development of backward districts through structured support and engagement with States/UTs.

faqs.q: Which of the following functionally divides the NITI Aayog to examine sectoral issues and priorities for national development?
The National Institute of Labour Economics Research and Development (NILERD) was formerly known as which of the following?
Under which Act was the Institute of Applied Manpower Research (IAMR) established in 1962?
In which year was the Institute of Applied Manpower Research (IAMR) renamed as NILERD?
NILERD is best described as which type of body under the NITI Aayog?
In which year did NILERD move to its own campus at Narela?
In which year was the Programme Evaluation Organization established to carry out independent impact evaluation of Central Government funded programmes?
faqs.e: This body was later merged into the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO) in 2015.

faqs.q: In which year was the Independent Evaluation Office established to accord more functional autonomy to the programme evaluation mechanism?
The Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO) was established in 2015 by merging which two bodies?

options.a: Programme Evaluation Organization and Independent Evaluation Office
options.d: Planning Commission and National Development Council

faqs.a: Programme Evaluation Organization and Independent Evaluation Office

faqs.q: The DMEO functions as which type of body in relation to the NITI Aayog?
Till 2017, the DMEO had how many Regional Development Monitoring and Evaluation Offices (RDMEOs)?
faqs.e: These were closed in 2017 and their staff transferred to DMEO Headquarters in New Delhi.

faqs.q: In which month and year was the erstwhile Planning Commission established?
The erstwhile Planning Commission was established on the recommendation of the Advisory Planning Board, which was constituted in which year?
Who was the chairman of the Advisory Planning Board constituted in 1946, on whose recommendation the Planning Commission was established?
Which of the following positions was the de facto executive (full-time functional) head of the erstwhile Planning Commission?

Consider the following statements regarding the composition of the erstwhile Planning Commission:
(I) The Prime Minister was its chairman.
(II) The commission had four to seven full-time expert members.
(III) State governments had guaranteed representation on the commission.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: The erstwhile Planning Commission was wholly a Centre-constituted body; state governments were not represented in it in any way.

faqs.q: Which committee/body of India's Administrative Reforms described the erstwhile Planning Commission as having earned the reputation of a "Parallel Cabinet" and sometimes a "Super Cabinet"?
faqs.e: This observation was made in the Interim Report on the Machinery for Planning, 1967.

faqs.q: Which constitutional expert observed that "Planning has superseded the federation and our country is functioning like a unitary system in many respects"?
P.V. Rajamannar, who observed an overlapping of functions between the erstwhile Planning Commission and the Finance Commission, was the Chairman of which Finance Commission?
In which month and year was the National Development Council (NDC) established?
The National Development Council was established on the recommendation of which document?

options.b: The First Five Year Plan (draft outline)
options.c: The Interim Report on the Machinery for Planning

faqs.a: The First Five Year Plan (draft outline)

faqs.q: Like the erstwhile Planning Commission, the National Development Council is which type of body?

options.a: Both a constitutional and a statutory body
options.d: Neither a constitutional nor a statutory body

faqs.a: Neither a constitutional nor a statutory body

faqs.q: Since which year have all Union Cabinet Ministers been included as members of the National Development Council?
When was the last (57th) meeting of the National Development Council held, and for what purpose?

options.a: 15 August 2014, to approve the Planning Commission's dissolution
options.b: 1 January 2015, to approve NITI Aayog's formation

faqs.q: The National Human Rights Commission is which type of body?
Under which legislation was the National Human Rights Commission established in 1993?

options.a: The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
options.b: The National Human Rights Commission Act, 1993
options.c: The Commission for Human Rights Act, 1993

faqs.a: The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the objectives of establishing the National Human Rights Commission:
(I) To strengthen institutional arrangements through which human rights issues could be addressed in a more focussed manner.
(II) To look into allegations of excesses independently of the government.
(III) To replace all existing statutory human rights bodies at the state level.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
Who should the Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission be?

options.a: A sitting judge of the Supreme Court only
options.b: A retired Chief Justice of India or a judge of the Supreme Court
options.c: A retired Chief Justice of a High Court
options.d: A sitting Chief Justice of India

faqs.a: A retired Chief Justice of India or a judge of the Supreme Court

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of the National Human Rights Commission:
(I) It consists of a chairperson and five members.
(II) At least one of the three "knowledge or practical experience" members must be a woman.
(III) It has seven ex-officio members, including the chairpersons of the National Commission for Minorities and National Commission for SCs.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
Who heads the six-member committee that recommends the appointment of the Chairperson and members of the National Human Rights Commission?
Appointment of a sitting judge of the Supreme Court or a sitting Chief Justice of a High Court to the National Human Rights Commission requires consultation with whom?
The chairperson and members of the National Human Rights Commission hold office for a term of three years or until they attain what age, whichever is earlier?
After their tenure, the chairperson and members of the National Human Rights Commission are ineligible for which of the following?

options.a: Further employment under the Central or a state government
options.c: Appointment as judges of the Supreme Court

faqs.a: Further employment under the Central or a state government

faqs.q:
Consider the following grounds on which the President can remove the chairperson or a member of the National Human Rights Commission:
(I) If he/she is adjudged insolvent.
(II) If he/she engages in any paid employment outside the duties of the office during the term.
(III) If he/she is absent from three consecutive meetings of the Commission without leave.
Which of the above is/are valid grounds for removal under the Act?
faqs.e: Absence from consecutive meetings is a removal ground for the National Commission for Women, not the NHRC.

faqs.q: On the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity, the President can remove the chairperson or a member of the National Human Rights Commission only after referring the matter to which authority for inquiry?
Who determines the salaries, allowances and other conditions of service of the chairperson or a member of the National Human Rights Commission?
Which of the following is a function of the National Human Rights Commission?

options.a: To inquire into any violation of human rights by a public servant, suo motu or on a petition
options.b: To appoint judges to Human Rights Courts
options.c: To try and convict violators of human rights
options.d: To award monetary compensation directly enforceable against the government

faqs.a: To inquire into any violation of human rights by a public servant, suo motu or on a petition

faqs.q: Where is the headquarters of the National Human Rights Commission located?
The National Human Rights Commission is not empowered to inquire into a matter after the expiry of how long from the date of the alleged violation?

Consider the following statements regarding the role of the National Human Rights Commission:
(I) Its functions are mainly recommendatory in nature.
(II) It has the power to punish violators of human rights directly.
(III) Its recommendations are not binding on the concerned government or authority.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: The Commission has no power to punish violators; it can only recommend action.

faqs.q: With respect to violations of human rights by members of the armed forces, the Central Government must inform the National Human Rights Commission of action taken on its recommendations within what period?
In general (non-armed-forces) cases, the concerned government or authority must inform the National Human Rights Commission about the action taken on its recommendations within what period?
Which of the following Amendment Acts made a person who has been a judge of the Supreme Court eligible for appointment as Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission?

options.c: The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2006
options.d: The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019

faqs.a: The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019

faqs.q: The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019 reduced the term of the chairperson and members of the National Human Rights Commission from five years to how many years?
The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019 increased the number of "knowledge or practical experience" members of the National Human Rights Commission from two to how many?

Who exercises all administrative and financial powers of the National Human Rights Commission (except judicial functions and the power to make regulations), subject to the control of the chairperson, as per the 2019 Amendment Act?
Under which legislation is provision made for the constitution of a State Human Rights Commission?

options.b: The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
options.c: The State Human Rights Commission Act, 1993
options.d: The National Human Rights Commission Act, 1993

faqs.a: The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993

faqs.q: A State Human Rights Commission can inquire into violation of human rights only in respect of subjects mentioned in which Lists of the Seventh Schedule?
If a case is already being inquired into by the National Human Rights Commission or any other Statutory Commission, what happens to that case at the State Human Rights Commission?

options.a: The matter is referred to the Supreme Court
options.b: The State Human Rights Commission does not inquire into that case
options.c: The State Commission's inquiry takes precedence
options.d: It is inquired into simultaneously by both

faqs.a: The State Human Rights Commission does not inquire into that case

faqs.q: The Central Government may confer human rights functions relating to Union Territories upon State Human Rights Commissions, except for which Union Territories?
faqs.e: The original provision excluded Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh; functions relating to human rights in the UT of Delhi are dealt with by the National Human Rights Commission.

faqs.q: Who should the Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission be?

options.a: A retired judge of the Supreme Court only
options.b: A retired Chief Justice or a Judge of a High Court
options.d: A retired Chief Justice of India

faqs.a: A retired Chief Justice or a Judge of a High Court

faqs.q: A person appointed as a member of a State Human Rights Commission on the basis of District Judge experience must have a minimum of how many years' experience as District Judge?
Who appoints the chairperson and members of a State Human Rights Commission?

options.b: Chief Justice of the High Court

faqs.q: Who heads the committee that recommends appointments to a State Human Rights Commission?

options.b: Chief Justice of the High Court

faqs.q: In a state having a Legislative Council, which additional members are included in the committee that recommends appointments to the State Human Rights Commission?

options.a: The Deputy Chairman of the Council only
options.b: Chairman of the Council and the leader of the opposition in the Council
options.c: The Advocate General of the State

faqs.a: Chairman of the Council and the leader of the opposition in the Council

faqs.q: Although appointed by the Governor, the chairperson and members of a State Human Rights Commission can be removed only by whom?

options.a: Chief Justice of the High Court

faqs.q: The chairperson and members of a State Human Rights Commission hold office for a term of three years or until they attain what age, whichever is earlier?
Who determines the salaries, allowances and other conditions of service of the chairperson or a member of a State Human Rights Commission?
A State Human Rights Commission is not empowered to inquire into a matter after the expiry of how long from the date of the alleged violation?

Consider the following statements regarding the role of a State Human Rights Commission:
(I) Its functions are mainly recommendatory in nature.
(II) Its recommendations are binding on the state government.
(III) It must be informed of action taken on its recommendations within one month.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: The Commission's recommendations, like those of the NHRC, are not binding on the concerned government or authority.

faqs.q: The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 provides for the establishment of a Human Rights Court at which level?
A Human Rights Court can be set up by the state government only with the concurrence of which authority?

options.a: The Chief Justice of the High Court of that state

faqs.a: The Chief Justice of the High Court of that state

faqs.q: For every Human Rights Court, an advocate appointed as special public prosecutor must have practiced for a minimum of how many years?
In which year did the Committee on Status of Women in India first recommend the constitution of a National Commission for Women?
In which year was the National Commission for Women actually constituted?
Under which legislation was the National Commission for Women established?

options.b: The National Commission for Women Act, 1992
options.c: The National Commission for Women Act, 1990
options.d: The Protection of Women's Rights Act, 1992

faqs.a: The National Commission for Women Act, 1990

faqs.q: The National Commission for Women is which type of body?
Which Ministry serves as the nodal ministry for the National Commission for Women?

options.a: Ministry of Women and Child Development
options.b: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

faqs.a: Ministry of Women and Child Development

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of the National Commission for Women:
(I) It consists of a chairperson, five members and a member-secretary.
(II) At least one member each should belong to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
(III) All members must be sitting or retired High Court judges.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: Members are drawn from persons with experience in law, trade unionism, industry, voluntary organisations, administration, and similar fields — not exclusively judicial backgrounds.

faqs.q: Who nominates the chairperson, members and member-secretary of the National Commission for Women?

options.d: Central Government (Ministry of Women and Child Development)

faqs.a: Central Government (Ministry of Women and Child Development)

faqs.q: The chairperson and members of the National Commission for Women hold office for a term of how many years?

Consider the following grounds for removal of the chairperson or a member of the National Commission for Women by the Central Government:
(I) Becoming an undischarged insolvent.
(II) Absence from three consecutive meetings of the Commission without leave.
(III) Conviction for an offence involving moral turpitude.
Which of the above is/are valid grounds for removal?
The functions of the National Commission for Women are provided under a mandate of how many points?
Which of the following is a function of the National Commission for Women?

options.a: To draft the national budget for women's welfare schemes
options.b: To fund litigation involving issues affecting a large body of women
options.c: To try cases of crimes against women in a Human Rights Court
options.d: To appoint judges to Family Courts

faqs.a: To fund litigation involving issues affecting a large body of women

faqs.q: To whom does the National Commission for Women present its annual report?
While investigating any matter, the National Commission for Women has all the powers of which of the following?

options.a: A civil court trying a suit
options.d: A criminal court trying a case

faqs.a: A civil court trying a suit

faqs.q: Which landmark Supreme Court judgement mandated that every employer provide effective complaints procedures and remedies, including compensation, for sexual harassment at the workplace?

options.a: Maneka Gandhi vs. Union of India
options.b: Indra Sawhney vs. Union of India

faqs.e: This 1997 judgement directly informs the National Commission for Women's handling of workplace sexual harassment complaints.

faqs.q: What is the Parivarik Mahila Lok Adalat (PMLA), evolved by the National Commission for Women, modelled on?
The Parivarik Mahila Lok Adalat primarily supplements the efforts of which authority for redressal of marriage and family affairs pending in courts?
Which of the following is an objective of the Parivarik Mahila Lok Adalat?

options.a: To appoint women judges to High Courts
options.b: To try criminal cases of dowry death
options.c: To provide speedy and cost-free dispensation of justice to women

faqs.a: To provide speedy and cost-free dispensation of justice to women

faqs.q: In which year did the Department of Women and Child Development become a separate Ministry of the Government of India?
The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights is which type of body?
Under which legislation was the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights set up?

options.a: The Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
options.b: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2007
options.d: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection) Act, 2005

faqs.a: The Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005

faqs.q: In which year was the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights actually set up?
Under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005, 'child rights' includes the rights adopted in which UN Convention?

options.a: UN Convention on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights
options.b: UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
options.d: UN Convention on Civil and Political Rights

faqs.a: UN Convention on the Rights of the Child

faqs.q: On which date did India ratify the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child?
faqs.e: The Convention itself was adopted by the UN on 20 November 1989; India ratified it later, on 11 December 1992.

faqs.q: Under the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, a child is defined as a human being below what age?
The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights operates under the administrative control of which Ministry?

options.c: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
options.d: Ministry of Women and Child Development

faqs.a: Ministry of Women and Child Development

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights:
(I) It consists of a Chairperson and six members.
(II) At least two of the six members should be women.
(III) The Chairperson is appointed on the recommendation of a five-member selection committee.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: The Chairperson is appointed on the recommendation of a three-member selection committee, not a five-member one.

faqs.q: Who chairs the three-member selection committee that recommends the Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights?

options.b: Minister-in-charge of the Ministry/Department of Women and Child Development

faqs.a: Minister-in-charge of the Ministry/Department of Women and Child Development

faqs.q: The Chairperson and members of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights hold office for a term of how many years?
A member of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights is not eligible for appointment for more than how many terms?
What is the upper age limit for holding office as Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights?
What is the upper age limit for holding office as a member of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights?
Who can remove the Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity?
Which of the following is a function of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights?

options.a: To appoint judges to Children's Courts
options.b: To frame the national education policy
options.c: To inquire into violation of child rights and recommend initiation of proceedings
options.d: To try offences against children in a special court

faqs.a: To inquire into violation of child rights and recommend initiation of proceedings

faqs.q: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights is prohibited from inquiring into a matter that is pending before which authority?

options.a: A State Commission for Protection of Child Rights or any other Statutory Commission
options.b: The National Human Rights Commission only

faqs.a: A State Commission for Protection of Child Rights or any other Statutory Commission

faqs.q: While inquiring into any matter, the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights has all the powers of which of the following?

options.a: A quasi-judicial commission with advisory powers only
options.b: A civil court trying a suit
options.c: A criminal court trying a case

faqs.a: A civil court trying a suit

faqs.q: To whom does the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights present its annual or special reports?

options.a: Central Government and the State Government concerned

faqs.a: Central Government and the State Government concerned

faqs.q: Under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights is assigned which of the following additional functions?

options.b: To appoint teachers in government schools
options.c: To inquire into complaints relating to a child's right to free and compulsory education

faqs.a: To inquire into complaints relating to a child's right to free and compulsory education

faqs.q: Under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights is assigned which of the following additional functions?

options.a: To grant bail in POCSO cases
options.b: To appoint Special Courts under the Act
options.d: To monitor the implementation of the provisions of the Act

faqs.a: To monitor the implementation of the provisions of the Act

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the additional functions of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights under the RTE Act, 2009, POCSO Act, 2012, and Juvenile Justice Act, 2015:
(I) Under all three Acts, the Commission monitors implementation of the respective Act's provisions.
(II) While inquiring into matters under POCSO and the Juvenile Justice Act, the Commission has the same powers as under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005.
(III) The Commission's activities under POCSO and the Juvenile Justice Act must be included in its annual report under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
Under which Act is provision made for the creation of a State Commission for Protection of Child Rights?

options.a: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2007
options.c: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection) Act, 2015
options.d: The Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005

faqs.a: The Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005

faqs.q: How may a state government constitute a State Commission for Protection of Child Rights?

options.a: Through a state legislative enactment only
options.c: Through an executive order of the Governor

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of a State Commission for Protection of Child Rights:
(I) It consists of a chairperson and six members.
(II) At least two of the six members should be women.
(III) The chairperson is appointed on the recommendation of a three-member selection committee chaired by the Chief Minister.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: The selection committee recommending the chairperson is chaired by the Minister-in-charge of the Department dealing with children, not the Chief Minister.

faqs.q: Who appoints the chairperson and members of a State Commission for Protection of Child Rights?

options.d: Chief Justice of the High Court

faqs.q: The chairperson and members of a State Commission for Protection of Child Rights hold office for a term of how many years?
What is the upper age limit for holding office as chairperson of a State Commission for Protection of Child Rights?
What is the upper age limit for holding office as a member of a State Commission for Protection of Child Rights?
To whom does a chairperson or member of a State Commission for Protection of Child Rights address a resignation?

options.d: Chief Justice of the High Court

faqs.q: Which of the following is a function of a State Commission for Protection of Child Rights?

options.a: To sanction the state child welfare budget
options.b: To appoint the state's Director of School Education
options.c: To inquire into violation of child rights and recommend initiation of proceedings in such cases
options.d: To try offences against children directly

faqs.a: To inquire into violation of child rights and recommend initiation of proceedings in such cases

faqs.q: While inquiring into any matter, a State Commission for Protection of Child Rights has all the powers of which of the following?

options.a: A civil court trying a suit
options.b: A criminal court trying a case

faqs.a: A civil court trying a suit

faqs.q: To whom does a State Commission for Protection of Child Rights submit its annual or special reports?

options.a: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights

faqs.q: The Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005 provides for the establishment of Children's Courts for the speedy trial of which of the following?

options.d: Offences against children or violation of child rights

faqs.a: Offences against children or violation of child rights

faqs.q: A Children's Court can be set up by the state government only with the concurrence of which authority?

options.a: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
options.b: The Chief Justice of the High Court of that state

faqs.a: The Chief Justice of the High Court of that state

faqs.q: For every Children's Court, an advocate appointed as special public prosecutor must have practiced for a minimum of how many years?
In which year was the Minorities Commission first set up by the Government of India through an executive resolution?
Which Ministry issued the 1978 resolution setting up the Minorities Commission?

options.d: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

faqs.q: Under which Act did the Minorities Commission become a statutory body and get renamed the National Commission for Minorities?

options.c: The National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992
options.d: The National Commission for Minorities (Amendment) Act, 1995

faqs.a: The National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992

faqs.q: In which year was the first statutory National Commission for Minorities constituted?
The National Commission for Minorities works under the administrative control of which Ministry?

options.c: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding minority communities notified under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992:
(I) The Act itself defines the term 'minority'.
(II) The Centre in 1993 notified Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Zoroastrians as minority communities.
(III) The Jain community was added to the notified list in 2014.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: The Act does not define 'minority' but enables the Central Government to notify minorities for the purposes of the Act.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of the National Commission for Minorities:
(I) It consists of a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and five members.
(II) Five members, including the Chairperson, should be from amongst the minority communities.
(III) Members are nominated by a collegium headed by the Chief Justice of India.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: The Chairperson and members are nominated by the Central Government, not a judicial collegium.

faqs.q: Before the National Commission for Minorities (Amendment) Act, 1995, the Commission consisted of a Chairperson and how many members?
Which position was added to the National Commission for Minorities by the National Commission for Minorities (Amendment) Act, 1995?
The chairperson and members of the National Commission for Minorities hold office for a period of how many years?

Consider the following grounds on which the Central Government can remove the Chairperson or a member of the National Commission for Minorities:
(I) Becoming an undischarged insolvent.
(II) Absence from three consecutive meetings of the Commission without leave.
(III) Conviction for an offence involving moral turpitude.
Which of the above is/are valid grounds for removal?
The National Commission for Minorities is provided with a mandate of how many functions?
Which of the following is a function of the National Commission for Minorities?

options.a: To draft the national minorities budget
options.b: To try cases of communal violence directly
options.c: To evaluate the progress of the development of minorities under the Union and States
options.d: To appoint judges to minority welfare boards

faqs.a: To evaluate the progress of the development of minorities under the Union and States

faqs.q: While evaluating, monitoring, or inquiring into a complaint, the National Commission for Minorities has all the powers of which of the following?

options.a: A civil court trying a suit
options.b: A criminal court trying a case

faqs.a: A civil court trying a suit

faqs.q: To whom does the National Commission for Minorities present its annual report?
